abstract: AbstractThis presentation demonstrates the impact of workflow automation in chemical engineering, highlighting how life sciences companies automate molecular and quantum dynamics analysis in pharmaceutical development. Using Rescale and Nextflow, a Fortune 500 life sciences customer saved time by automating manual data management, reduced duplication and re-work, and ultimately sped up the drug development timeline. By making complex workflows easier and more efficient, the customer reduces R&D costs and delivers new medicines to market faster, with greater confidence in their efficacy for patients.Rescale works with leading life sciences companies to build digital threads that transform pharmaceutical development by connecting teams and automating complex scientific workflows. Digital threads play a central role in life sciences R&D, linking each step of the drug discovery process, from modeling simulation to data analysis, making it faster and easier for global teams from different disciplines to collaborate seamlessly from anywhere. Digital threads also provide a trace of the specific steps involved in producing consistent results, with modularity for teams to use their best-fit software and hardware technologies.Using Rescale and Nextflow to build computational workflows for multi-step analyses, the example life sciences company provides their scientists and researchers with a digital thread of processes, data, and tools so they focus on answering key research questions. This approach improves accessibility and reproducibility of complex workflows critical for faster turnarounds in collaborative research, while enabling them to swap in any preferred commercial, open-source, and custom technologies. With Rescale and Nextflow, any collaborator can quickly automate chains of analysis from a variety of applications and teams involved have visibility of their process and data for greater speed and confidence in decision-making.

abstract: AbstractWorkshop Format:Duration: 2 hoursStructure:Short Presentation (15 minutes):The workshop will kick off with a brief presentation highlighting the current challenges facing pharma industry and the landscape of modeling and simulations and their potential benefits in process development and manufacturing.Panel Discussion (90 minutes):Following the presentation, a panel discussion will feature experts from various sectors:Pharmaceutical Industry: Leaders who have integrated modeling and simulations into their development pipelines.Academia: Researchers contributing to advancements in computational sciences and data-driven methodologies.Modeling Software Companies: Innovators providing cutting-edge simulation tools that power digital transformation.The discussion will focus on key topics such as:How can we democratize access to advanced modeling and simulation tools for non-modelers in our organizations?Current obstacles in implementing these technologies in process development, including the skills gap, high costs, and resistance to change.Collaboration models between industry, academia, and software companies to accelerate innovation and address key challenges.Future trends and opportunities in leveraging data science, AI, and digital twins to further enhance process development and manufacturing.

abstract: AbstractThe Purdue Center for Operations and Optimization in Process Systems (COOPS) is at the forefront of transforming the field of process systems engineering. By leveraging cutting-edge research and fostering innovation, COOPS aims to enhance the efficiency, sustainability, and safety of various industries.Our center focuses on:- conducting state-of-the-art research combining modeling and theoretical studies to solve complex systems engineering problems- engaging students at all levels (undergraduate, MS, and PhD) in hands-on research and specialized courses to prepare the next generation of leaders in PSE- providing expert consultation and innovative solutions for industrial challenges, ensuring our research to have practical impact- collaborate with other faculty and departments in Purdue University to promote interdisciplinary research and educationOur mission is to drive innovation and excellence in various critical areas, including process operations and control, scheduling, smart manufacturing, crystallization, predictive maintenance, energy systems optimization, life cycle analysis, process design, supply chain optimization, artificial intelligence, and quantum computing.

abstract: AbstractBreakthrough and static adsorption measurements are important for the development materials used in direct air capture (DAC) of carbon dioxide. These techniques are particularly valuable for evaluating material performance in low CO2 concentrations and in the presence of water. By utilizing these analytical methods, researchers can reduce the development time of new materials and processes for DAC, by measuring surface texture, adsorption capacity, and selectivity.
